1. This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [for short, the 'M.V. Act'] filed by the Original Claimants, being not satisfied by the compensation awarded by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Aurangabad [hereinafter referred to as the 'learned Tribunal'], in M.A.C.P. No. 675 of 2014 [for short, the 'Claim Petition'], decided by the Judgment and Award dated 22.11.2016, the operative part of which reads as follows :
"1] The petition is partly allowed with proportionate costs. 2] Respondent Nos.1 to 3 jointly and severally deposit within a period of two months from the date of this order an amount of Rs.5,62,000/- (Rupees Five Lacs Sixty Two Thousand only) towards compensation together with interest thereon @ 9% per annum, from the date of filing of this petition till its realization, including the NFL amount of Rs.50,000/-.
3] After depositing the amount, it be apportioned as under : -
Claimant Nos. 1 & 2 - Rs. 2,50,000/- each, Claimant No. 3 - Rs.62,000/-
The amounts be paid to the Claimants by account cheques.
4. Award be drawn accordingly."
2. In this Appeal, Respondent Nos. 1 and 3 are represented by their respective Advocates.
Respondent No. 2, who is the owner of the offending vehicle i.e. Truck, is served with the initial notice, however, no one has appeared on his behalf.

Considering the issue involved in the matter, it is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, the Appeal can be finally heard at the stage of admission, to which the SG Punde 3 FA520.2019.odt learned Advocate for the Insurance Company agreed.
Notice of final hearing issued to Respondent No. 2 is awaited.

According to the learned Advocate for Respondent No. 3 - Insurance Company, the impugned Judgment and Award was made jointly and severally against the Insurance Company and the Vehicle Owner, and the Insurance Company has satisfied the Award as the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No. 3 and the Appeal is confined to the legal aspects which are covered by Judicial Pronouncements and the Appeal can be disposed off in view of the above submissions.
3.
In view of the above, the Appeal is heard finally.

4. The facts in brief giving rise to the present Appeal are as follows : -

sentences.text:
The Appellants, who are the parents and sister of Pradeep Prakash Bhalerao (hereinafter referred to as 'the Deceased'), filed the Claim Petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, contending that the Deceased, while traveling on Motorcycle No.
MH-20/CX-5980 from Aurangabad to Sillod, had reached near Naigavhan Bus Stand, when a Truck bearing No. MH-19/J-3628, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, gave dash to the motorcycle of the Deceased, and the accident took place.
The Deceased succumbed to the accidental injuries.
They claimed compensation of Rs. 12.00 Lakh along with other benefits.
SG Punde 4 FA520.2019.odt 5.
The said Claim Petition was contested by Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 by filing a Written Statement below Exh. 12.
The Respondent No.3 - the Insurance Company contested the Claim Petition by filing a Written Statement below Exh. 16.
They denied the Claim.
6. The learned Tribunal framed the issues below Exh. 17.
The Appellants led the evidence and brought on record the relevant documents.
No witness was examined by the Respondents.
Upon appreciating the evidence available on record, the learned Tribunal passed the impugned Judgment and Award.

7. The learned Advocate for the Appellants submitted that the learned Tribunal wrongly applied the multiplier by considering the age of the parents of the Deceased, instead of applying the multiplier on the basis of the age of the Deceased.
He further submits that there is no addition towards the future prospects and no amount towards Consortium has been awarded by the learned Tribunal.

He submits that the impugned Award be modified accordingly in light of the settled position in the cases of Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., 2009 AIR(SC) 3104, National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, 2019 (4) Mh.L.J. 1.
SG Punde 5 FA520.2019.odt 8.

sentences.text: The learned Advocate for Respondent No. 3 - Insurance Company submits that there is no dispute regarding the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the above-referred three Judgments.

He submits that, there cannot be any dispute that while considering the multiplier in the case of a Deceased, who is major by age, the age of the Deceased is required to be taken into consideration for applying the multiplier.
Likewise, future prospects applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case are required to be considered, along with the Consortium.
He further submits that the learned Tribunal granted interest @ 9% p.a., which is on the higher side, and that the same needs to be modified and made 6% p.a.
He submits that the Appeal can be disposed off in light of the submissions made by both the sides.
9. Perused the impugned Judgment and Award.

The learned Tribunal, while applying the multiplier,
considered the age of the parents and applied the a multiplier of 11.

However, considering the age of Prakash Rangnath Bhalerao And Ors vs Abdul Gaffar Abdul Majid And Ors on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8924294/
3 the Deceased at the time of the accident, i.e. 23 years, the multiplier of 18 would be applicable in view of the above-referred judgment in Sarla Verma (supra).

sentences.text: As the Deceased was not in permanent employment and was self-employed and below the age of 40 years, 40% of the monthly income considered by the learned Tribunal will have to be added towards the future prospects as per the above-referred judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra).

As regards the Consortium is concerned, it would be Rs.40,000/-
SG Punde 6 FA520.2019.odt each for the parents of the Deceased towards Filial consortium, as per the judgment in Magma (supra).
10.

Admittedly, the Award passed by the learned Tribunal has not been challenged by the Insurance Company by filing appropriate proceedings and hence, the contentions in respect of the higher rate of interest by the learned Tribunal need no consideration.

living expenses @ 50%

(Rs. 58,800 x 18)
9.

A. Loss of parental consortium to both parents @ 40,000/- each= Rs.80,000/-
B.

Funeral expenses = Rs.15,000/-
C. Loss of estate = Rs. 15,000/-

10. Total compensation (pecuniary + non-pecuniary) Rs. 11,68,400/-
(Rs. 10,58,400/- + Rs. 1,10,000/- = Rs. 11,68,400/-)
